jobs.description: Employer: Council for Court Excellence Expires: 11/05/2026 The Council for Court Excellence (CCE) is a non-profit organization that brings people together to conduct research, educate, and advocate to make D.C.’s unique legal systems more just, equitable, and accountable to the community. For students who are not receiving course credit or other funding for their internship, CCE will provide interns with a stipend of up to $2500 depending on hours worked. CCE also covers public transportation costs to and from required meetings or events. Availability CCE offers hybrid work opportunities (at our office located in downtown Washington, DC, in a location of your choice, or some combination); we often host events in the office or in DC, so we prefer locally based interns. We offer three internship sessions that align with the academic calendar: Spring (from January to May), Summer (from June to August), and Fall (from September to December). jobs.title: Applied Scientist (Economics) Intern at Zillow
jobs.description: Employer: Zillow Expires: 11/05/2026 About the teamThe forecasting and business economics group at Zillow shapes planning and drives decision making across Zillow’s businesses. Embedded in the finance organization, our team prioritizes research projects that directly impact the company’s bottom line and growth. We bring together forecasters, economists, applied scientists, data scientists, and data visualization engineers to build forecasts and craft research that elevates how our businesses operate. We transform our industry-leading data with our expertise in statistics and economics into actionable insights that inform decisions at every level of the company. Our work combines state of the art quantitative methods across forecasting, data science, and causal inference to help answer practical questions for our business leaders.About the roleAt Zillow, interns do meaningful work that contributes to the business from day one. Our 9 week summer internship program, running June 14th through August 13th, gives students the opportunity to bring their ideas and perspectives to real projects alongside Zillow teams.Interns build hands-on experience, connect with mentors and leaders, and take part in learning and community experiences with their intern cohort. Our 2027 internships are based in Seattle and follow a hybrid schedule, with interns generally working together in person Tuesday through Thursday. Eligible interns will receive a stipend to help offset summer housing and relocation costs. We’re looking for students who are analytical and detail-oriented with the ability to create structure from ambiguity. You have an intense curiosity to learn and can do so in a fast-paced dynamic environment. If you are not afraid of working with large amounts of data, you’ll get the chance to make it all come together into meaningful metrics used to make strategic business decisions.During your internship, you will have opportunities to: Partner with your manager and stakeholders to translate open-ended business questions into an analytical approach, with clear deliverables that will directly translate to tangible benefits to revenue. Explore, clean, and validate housing, economic, business, or financial data; document assumptions and identify data-quality issues.Build and compare models to support prediction and forecasting.Transform observational data into causal models using clever identificationDesign experiments to improve how we price and operate across our different businesses Evaluate models using appropriate baselines and time-based validation, and communicate uncertainty, limitations, and trade-offs.Investigate trends, forecast errors, and drivers of business performance to develop actionable insights.Create reproducible analyses, visualizations, or reporting workflows that help partners understand and use your findings.Share your approach, results, and recommendations with technical and nontechnical audiences, and document your work for a clear handoff.Who you areCurrently pursuing a Masters or PhD in statistics, economics, data science, applied mathematics, quantitative finance, or a related quantitative field, with an expected graduation between December 2027 and Summer 2028. Strong foundation in probability, statistics, and regression analysis, with exposure to econometrics. Specifically time-series and causal analysis through coursework and research experience.Use AI tools to accelerate and expand their work without outsourcing their own thinking to it.Can use Python or similar to prepare data, conduct analysis, and build models. Even if you’re not writing code anymore, we expect an ability to express statistical concepts clearly through pseudocode and think through edgecases when designing systems. Can explain analytical findings clearly and collaborate with people who bring different perspectives and expertise including non technical stakeholders.Move quickly and ambitiously without sacrificing attention to detail; enjoy zooming in and out based on context. Approach problems thoughtfully: you check your assumptions, validate results, and distinguish what the data supports from what remains uncertain.Are interested in applying quantitative methods to housing markets, business forecasting, and financial decision-making.Get to know usAt Zillow, we’re reimagining how people move—through the real estate market and through their careers. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help people navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.How we work is a key part of that transformation. It’s an exciting time to work for Idaho Power. Our work plays a critical role in communities we serve across Idaho and Oregon, and we’re working hard to provide our customers with the safe, reliable, affordable energy they depend on. In addition to the meaningful work we do, we offer work-life balance, competitive pay and benefits, an employee incentive plan, and both a 401k employer-match and a pension plan, making Idaho Power one of the best employers in the state. What does a Construction Project Manager Intern do for us?Launch your career in construction project management by helping bring electric utility infrastructure projects to life. Working alongside an experienced team of project managers, the Construction Project Manager Intern will gain hands-on experience supporting projects from planning through construction and completion. The intern will collaborate with internal departments and external agencies, learn from project managers, construction managers, engineers and organizational leaders, and build practical skills in a dynamic mix of office and field settings. A COMPETITIVE CANDIDATE WILL HAVE Knowledge of:General knowledge of project management, construction, and engineering principlesDeveloping knowledge of electric utility facilities, design and construction processes, estimating, scheduling, cost tracking, quality, risk and the utility business environmentSkills in:Effective oral and written communicationTeamworkOrganizationAttention to detailData collection and analysisMeeting documentationBasic schedule and budget trackingThe use of Microsoft Office and related project management softwareAbility to:Work safely in office and field environmentsRead and develop a basic understanding of drawings, schedules, estimates, contracts and project recordsOrganize and prioritize assignmentsEstablish effective working relationshipsWork independently with direction and as part of a project teamIdentify issues and develop alternativesAnalyze project informationPrepare written and oral updatesManage multiple tasks and deadlinesMINIMUM REQUIREMENTSEducation:High school diploma or GEDCurrently enrolled in an accredited college or university program in construction management, project management, engineering, business or a related field as a junior, non-graduating senior status, or in a related advanced degree programExperience:N/ALicenses & Certifications:Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record based on driving requirements for the positionPHYSICAL REQUIREMENTSApproximately 70% of the work is performed in an office environment with computer use and phone conversation, requiring sitting up to 8 hours daily. This position may occasionally stand/walk on uneven surfaces of construction sites up to 8 hours (with periodic breaks) in different weather environments, while wearing PPE. Climbing of stairs and ladders is occasionally required in power generation facilities. Lifting/carrying of up to 20 lb. Crouching, kneeling, and stooping/bending is required occasionally. Driving of up to 4 hours throughout the IPC service area is required occasionally. The above is a summary of the primary essential functions of the position. This job may require the performance of additional tasks assigned by company leaders or management. Questions regarding job requirements or accommodation requests should be directed to Human Resources. ADDITIONAL INFORMATIONThe position will require construction site visits and outdoor work, including walking over uneven terrain and working in varying weather conditions. Required personal protective equipment and safety procedures must be followed. The position may have opportunities for overnight travel, limited to one night, for field visits. This is a Seasonal position and resumes annually (typically between May and October). No relocation benefits are provided. Internal, regular employees who are successful candidates will be placed as regular employees in a Temporary Duty Assignment job classification. In order for your current position to be held open for the duration of the assignment or filled temporarily, qualified employees must have supervisory approval to participate and have been in their current position for at least six months JOB COMPETENCIESAdaptability, Collaborating, Communication, Decision Making, Planning and Organizing, Work Standards To be considered for this position, please visit our website at www.idahopower.com/careers and complete our online application.All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex (including pregnancy), age, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, physical or mental disability, marital status, and any other status protected by applicable federal and state laws.If you have questions, or require assistance or accommodation to complete the online application, please contact us at: Phone: 208-388-2965 or Email: jobs@idahopower.comIdaho Power is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: COMMUNICATIONS STUDENT INTERN at Calleguas Municipal Water District
jobs.description: Employer: Calleguas Municipal Water District Expires: 11/06/2026 Student interns receive training and mentoring performing assignments that serve to offer practical experience and broad exposure to Calleguas Municipal Water District’s (Calleguas’s) organizational structure. This position supports the External Affairs Department, and tasks will primarily focus on efforts related to communications and public outreach, media strategies, videography, and legislative affairs.The student intern position is a part-time, temporary, at-will position limited to no greater than eight hours per day and 24 hours per week. Work schedule will be determined based upon department needs and the intern's school schedule. Work hours will typically be Monday through Friday during regular business hours, although some weekend work may be requested, such as attendance at community events. The length of time for an internship is six months but may be extended by the General Manager. Where possible, the District will cooperate with the intern’s college or university if the school intends to award class credits for student participation in an internship program.ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIESThe duties listed below are intended only as illustrations of the various types of work that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to this position. Student Intern• Participate in the development and implementation of departmental communications programs, including, but not limited to, social media, press releases, and fact sheets.• Support organization and execution of District facility tours for various audiences.• Produce a series of short videos highlighting employees in a specific department.• Analyze legislation and its potential impact on the District and / or its retail agencies.• Participate in relevant community events to expand knowledge of the water industry.• Support staff with public outreach activities, including participating in community events. This may include weekends depending on the event.• Prepare and provide reports and presentations.• Perform office duties and activities as required.• Perform other related Student Intern level job duties as required. SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIESThis position does not include supervisory responsibilities. QUALIFICATIONSTo perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Education and Experience• Current enrollment in a community college, undergraduate, or graduate degree program and in good standing with the college or university, or• Graduated within one year of date of application with a degree from a community college, undergraduate, or graduate degree program.Competencies• Experience or interest in the state and federal legislative processes.• Experience in creating, filming, editing and organizing brief but compelling explanatory videos.• Create spreadsheets, presentations, outreach materials, etc.• Assist in preparing and reviewing a variety of documents and correspondence for accuracy and completeness.• Understand and follow verbal and written instructions.• Communicate clearly and concisely, both verbally and in writing.• Operate typical office devices and equipment.• Experience with Microsoft Office and social media platforms.• Establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work. PHYSICAL AND MENTAL DEMANDSThe physical and mental requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by employees to successfully perform the essential functions of this class. Physical• Sitting, standing, bending, reaching, talking and hearing, in person, in meetings and by telephone.• Manual dexterity and use of hands and fingers to handle and feel sufficient to operate a District vehicle, computers and standard office machines, such as calculators, telephones, copiers, and scanners.• Normal range of hearing. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close and distance vision and the ability to adjust focus. May require lifting up to 25 pounds. Mental• Outstanding written and oral communication skills.• Interpretation and analysis of complex information and documents.• Perform highly detailed work on multiple, concurrent tasks with occasional interruptions.• Work under deadlines.• Interact with District executives and managers, governmental officials, employees, and the public.WORK ENVIRONMENTThe work environment characteristics are those generally encountered in an office environment. The employee works under typical office conditions, and the noise level is usually quiet. On occasion the Student Intern may visit District facilities located in Ventura County to collect video footage or attend offsite tours and events. SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS• Possess a California Motor Vehicle Operators License and proof of a good driving record, i.e., a driving record provided by the DMV showing less than 2 points assessed in the last 36 months and/or no serious or multiple traffic violations or accidents or failure to appear notices within the last 36 months.• Agree to authorize background reference checking with past employers and personal references.• Agree to submit to and pass the District’s pre-employment, post-offer medical examination performed by a physician chosen and paid for by the District. EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYERCalleguas Municipal Water District is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic information, pregnancy, gender identification or other protected characteristic as outlined in federal, state, or local laws. jobs.description: Employer: BlueGrace Logistics Expires: 11/07/2026 Please note that we will collect applications through September, and begin interviewing candidates in early fall for our Summer 2027 internship program!Who We Are: BlueGrace Logistics is one of the fastest growing Transportation Management companies in the US. Headquartered in Tampa, FL with 6 offices throughout the US and one recent expansion in Mexico. We help businesses better understand and optimize their supply chain by combining predictive analytics with advanced technology while empowering top talent who share our core values. jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Associated Universities (ORAU) Expires: 11/07/2026 The University of Tennessee - Oak Ridge Innovation Institute (UT-ORII) is seeking applications from undergraduate students currently enrolled in colleges and universities across the US who are interested in participating in its Science Alliance Student Mentoring and Research Training (SMaRT) Program. Students who will be rising sophomores, juniors and seniors in the Fall 2027 semester are eligible to apply. This prominent program will select approximately 40 qualified candidates to participate in a 10-week summer program scheduled from May 24 until July 31, 2027 (approximate dates). May 24-28th will be conducted virtually. As a selected intern, you will receive a funded internship, including stipends, housing and an allowance for travel to and from Knoxville, TN. You will be expected to attend all 10-weeks of the program. Time off for conferences, vacations, or other academic programs will not be allowed.You will engage in interdisciplinary research jointly administered by some of the nation’s top researchers from The University of Tennessee and Oak Ridge National Laboratory. Dedicated graduate student mentors will work closely with you, and through focused professional development activities you will prepare materials necessary to apply for future opportunities. This summer program will build your network, build your resume and prepare you for the next steps in your academic and professional career.Our program will provide research opportunities in the following areas:Transportation Mobility, Cybersecurity, and AutomationCircular Bioeconomy Systems, Environmental Science, Renewable and Recyclable Materials, Sustainable ManufacturingAdvanced Materials and Manufacturing, Materials in Extreme Environments, and Fusion Materials and Technology*Data science and engineering threads will be woven through each of these three areas.*Data science and engineering threads, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning, will be woven through each of these three areas.Benefits to you as a SMaRT Intern:The interdisciplinary atmosphere provided at UT-ORII will expose you to team science, an increasingly important platform for research. As an intern, you will also gain first-hand research experience in emerging fields (e.g. quantum information sciences and data sciences) while working with state-of-the-art research instruments. Together, these experiences will help prepare you for exciting and rewarding careers. Interns will prepare CVs, personal statements for future opportunities, as well as short research presentations and scientific posters that can be presented at conferences. Graduate student mentors will work closely with SMaRT interns and will be available to share their graduate school experiences. Overall, participation in the SMaRT Program will help you understand and evaluate your future career options, including in academia, national laboratories, and in the industries of the future.Stipends, Housing and Travel:The stipend will be $7,000 over 10 weeks. You will receive a one-time $250 credit on your VolCard to use toward eligible expenses.University of TN on-campus housing will be provided. Housing will be apartment style.Travel will be reimbursed for inbound and outbound expenses up to $1,200 for participants who live more than fifty miles, one-way, from the assigned hosting site. About the Oak Ridge Institute at The University of Tennessee (UT-ORII):The University of Tennessee (UT) and Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) have launched UT-ORII to foster interdisciplinary research and education. The primary goals of the institute are to: attract talent to East Tennessee and to develop a world-class STEM workforce that will, among other things, create and lead the industries of the future. UT-ORII brings together faculty, research scientists, students, and ORNL researchers to create a collaborative environment in which interdisciplinary discovery and creativity flourish.Click on the following links for the UT-ORII SMaRT Internship website and a video from the UT-ORII—2024 Summer Internship Program. Campagna has reserved office hours for drop-in visits related to these opportunities if you are local. His office is open to visitors after 3 p.m. EST each Friday. centers of influence and passive lead sources that can consistently generate referrals and opportunities.Identify new businesses, organizations, events, and community partnerships for the throughout the community.Represent Wyant Insurance & Financial Services professionally at all times.Track community marketing activity and the results generated from those efforts.Events & Community position will follow a clear, defined marketing schedule designed to ensure time is being spent intentionally and consistently.The weekly schedule will include designated time for:Field & Community MarketingCOI and Referral Partner DevelopmentSocial Media & Content CreationSEO & Microsite ManagementEvent Planning & Community InvolvementCanva & Marketing Material CreationTracking, Reporting & PlanningThere will be clear expectations around how much time should be spent out in the field versus working on social media, digital marketing, outreach, follow-up, and other responsibilities.Tracking, Accountability & Sales Team MeetingsAn important part of this position will be measuring what is actually working.The Marketing & Community Outreach Specialist will track both marketing activity and marketing results, including items such as businesses visited, COIs contacted, LinkedIn outreach, events attended, leads generated, referrals received, quote opportunities created, social media activity, and other relevant results.This person will regularly provide feedback during sales team meetings and help the team understand:What marketing strategies are workingWhat isn't generating resultsWhere leads and quotes are coming fromWhich relationships are producing referralsWhich events and community activities are worth continuingWhat messaging or approaches are generating conversationsWhat needs to be changed or improvedWhere the agency should focus its marketing efforts nextWe are looking for someone who is comfortable testing new ideas, measuring the results, receiving feedback, and continuously improving the agency's marketing approach.Success will not simply be measured by activity. Visiting 20 businesses or creating five social media posts only matters if those activities ultimately help create relationships, referrals, leads, quote opportunities, community awareness, and new business.What We're Looking ForThe ideal candidate is professional, outgoing, dependable, creative, organized, flexible, and comfortable starting conversations with new people.Because much of this position takes place outside of the office, this individual must also be self-motivated and capable of managing responsibilities independently while following the agency's established marketing plan.The ideal candidate should be:Timely and dependable, with excellent follow-through.Highly organized and capable of managing multiple relationships, events, campaigns, schedules, and follow-up activities.Outgoing and personable, with the confidence to walk into a local business, introduce themselves, and start building a relationship.Professional when representing Wyant Insurance & Financial Services.Comfortable using social media, LinkedIn, Canva, and digital marketing tools.Creative and comfortable taking photos and producing short-form video/Reel content.Comfortable working from a structured schedule and being accountable for measurable results.Able to communicate what is and isn't working and recommend adjustments.A team player who can coordinate with and help organize sales team members for events and community marketing activities.Results-oriented and motivated by generating new relationships, leads, referrals, and quote opportunities.Driving & Community TravelThis position requires frequent local travel throughout Richmond. The Marketing & Community Outreach Specialist will drive company-provided commercial/marketing vehicles while visiting businesses, attending events, and conducting community outreach.The agency will provide the vehicle and cover fuel expenses associated with approved business activities. Candidates must have a valid driver's license and an acceptable driving record.What Success Looks LikeSuccess in this role isn't measured simply by how many social media posts are created, businesses are visited, or events are attended. jobs.description: Employer: Nebraska Public Power District Expires: 11/07/2026 Apprentice Line Technician Intern - Distribution Summer 2027Kearney, NE, US, 68848-2170 Norfolk, NE, US, 68701-7227 Plattsmouth, NE, US, 68048-2062 South Sioux City, NE, US, 68776-0187 York, NE, US, 68467-0608 Nebraska Public Power District (NPPD) has an immediate opening for a Apprentice Line Technician Intern - Distribution Summer 2027 located out of the Kearney Operations Center in Kearney, NE, the Norfolk Operations Center in Norfolk, NE, the Plattsmouth Office in Plattsmouth, NE, the South Sioux City Office in South Sioux City, NE, and the York Operations Center Office in York, NE. Position closes October 31 at 11:59 p.m. Central Time. This position will report to the Distribution Supervisor for the respective location. Position SummaryThe Internship's function is to learn and mentor from experienced line technicians in the field for a period of time starting mid-May through mid-August 2027. Incumbent must have successfully completed their first year of school with an accredited institution in Utility Line and must be required to complete an internship as part of the program curriculum. The Internship student will climb wood poles to perform repairs, maintenance and construction duties as required to ensure effective operation of NPPD's Distribution and Subtransmission Grid system, in a safe and efficient manner. Incumbent must be certified to climb through courses offered at school. Some overnight travel will be required. A Class A CDL license is required prior to and throughout the duration of the internship program. Incumbent will be required to complete a background check, physical, and drug screen prior to starting with the District. Incumbent will be required to report wearing safety shoes that meet ASTM F2413-05 specifications. Incumbent must live within 30 minutes of your reporting office in accordance with OG-T&D-GU-029, Off-Duty Response Time Guidelines. Education, Training and ExperienceThe incumbent must have successfully completed the first semester of college in the Utility Line program at either Metro Community College or Northeast Community College. Incumbent must be certified to climb through an accredited institution.Licenses and/or CertificationsClass A CDL required at the start of employment.Essential Duties & ResponsibilitiesAscend and descend wood poles at any height to perform work as required in a safe and productive manner with supervision. Concentrate and be fully aware of responsibilities while on patrol of distribution and subtransmission lines within the grid system. Maintain favorable public relations with property owners, other District personnel, business establishments, and customers. Safely operate and maintain tools and equipment assigned, according to District policies and procedures. Operate and maintain mobile and hydraulic aerial equipment associated with construction and maintenance including digger derricks. Incumbent is accountable for miscellaneous other responsibilities as assigned or required.Accountable for other duties as assigned.Core CompetenciesCustomer FocusEmployees & Teamwork/Diversity & InclusionIntegrity/ExcellencePublic Service/Environmental StewardshipSafetySalary Information - Nebraska Public Power District offers a competitive starting salary with opportunities for growth. In addition to the base salary range listed below, NPPD employees may also be eligible for our Annual Incentive Program (AIP) that may supplement total compensation at a level above and beyond the stated salary range. Successful applicants will be provided more information regarding the incentive program at the time of an interview.Pay Grade - 99 HourlyTypical Pay Grade Starting Salary Range: $24.54/hour Interns will be eligilbe for $1000 housing stipend. Travel Required: Up to 25% (With no or minimal overnight stays, less than 3 per month, typically within state of Nebraska) Travel required may fluctuate by business need. This is an estimate and will be discussed further with candidates that receive an interview. If you are an individual with a disability and would like to request a reasonable accommodation as part of the employment selection process, please contact Human Resources at Nebraska Public Power District.Nebraska Public Power District is an Equal Opportunity EmployerWe are an Equal Opportunity Employer who values the contributions of its diverse work force. We are only legally able to hire persons who are 1) a United States citizen or national, 2) a lawful permanent resident of the United States, or 3) an alien legally authorized to work in the United States.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Change Academy Internship at Marketing for Change
jobs.description: Employer: Marketing for Change Expires: 11/07/2026 Spring 2027: Change Academy Internship & Fellowship (Orlando, FL & Alexandria, VA + Denver, CO is design only) DescriptionThe Change Academy at Marketing for Change offers graduate students, college seniors and others a paid semester-long experience working and learning at one of the nation’s leading behavior-change marketing agencies. In behavior-change marketing, the objective is not sales or profits; it’s influencing behaviors in a way that leads to a healthier, safer, more sustainable world. Each semester, the Change Academy accepts three to five interns with demonstrated skills or education in marketing, advertising, writing, research, and graphic design. Interns work together with experts in their field on real-life projects and also receive both skill-specific and broader training in behavioral science. Interns participate in agency events, client meetings and (if you want) off-the clock social gatherings. Interns earn $18.40 an hour or minimum wage (whichever is higher) and work 20 hours a week, with at least one day a week in our offices. The in-office experience is critical to help interns improve their skills, work with mentors and share a group experience with other interns in their cohort. Please confirm you can participate in person at your selected location. LocationOur offices are located in Orlando and just outside Washington, DC, and we very much prefer to hire people willing to locate in those areas. Additionally, we have a design hub in the Denver area. We are mostly a hybrid workforce with staff working together in-person at least one day a week because we value the fun and collaboration that allows. The program lasts between 12 and 16 weeks depending on the semester. Instruction takes place during the first 6 to 8 weeks of the internship, mixed with group projects and real work experience. The final weeks focus on work experience and give applicants an opportunity to build an impressive portfolio. Select interns may also be asked to apply as fellows, who can work up to 40 hours a week, or to join the Marketing for Change team permanently as employees. The Change Academy is the main path to entry-level employment at Marketing for Change. Several former M4C interns are now in leadership roles at M4C, including an art director, creative director, senior media planner, and strategist.Requirements Relevant experience or college classes in a related field. Preference is given to graduate students, recent graduates or college seniors with at least one prior internship in a relevant field. Other adults with the right skills but no degree may also apply. (Several have been successful in the past.)Deep curiosity in what makes people tick.An interest in using your powers for good and making the world a better place.Being a nice person. Seriously. We want the kind of person most other people love to work with. A quick note about our hiring processApplying for a job can feel a little like sending your application out into the void and hoping a real person is on the other side. At Marketing for Change, one will be. Real people on our team review every application. We may use technology to make parts of the process easier, but when it comes to getting to know you, considering what you could bring to our team and making hiring decisions, that’s us. We know there’s a real person on the other side of every application, too. Someone who gave us their time, shared a little bit of their story and decided we might be worth exploring. We don’t take that lightly. And if you’re considering us, we’re genuinely glad you’re here. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and Form I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification. Please submit your application by November 1, 2026, to be considered for this opportunity. We look forward to learning more about you! Location & TimingJanuary 2027 - May 2027 | Orlando, FL & Alexandria, VA + Denver, CO (design only)

jobs.title: CRM Consulting Internship (Spring 2027) at Eide Bailly
jobs.description: Employer: Eide Bailly Expires: 11/07/2026 We are looking for an intern to join our Technology Consulting team! Internship Duration: January - AprilMajors: Management Information Systems, Computer Science, Etc. Location: Lehi, Phoenix, Fargo, Denver, Fort Collins, Sioux Falls, or Billings Applicants must apply through the Eide Bailly portal to be considered.Who We AreEide Bailly is a Top 25 CPA and business advisory firm with over 50 offices in the U.S. and India. Since 1917, we’ve built our firm around one thing: people. We believe meaningful work starts with meaningful relationships — with our clients, our communities, and each other. That’s why we focus on creating an environment where you feel supported, connected, and empowered to grow. You’ll be part of a team that values authenticity, fosters trust, and provides you with the tools to thrive. Why You’ll Love Working HereYou’ll belong. We foster an inclusive, supportive environment where people look out for each other. You’re a valued part of the team from day one.You’ll grow. You’ll get hands-on experience with a variety of clients and industries or projects, all while working directly with experienced professionals who want you to succeed.You’ll be supported. Whether it’s your Eide Guide, Career Advisor, or a co-worker you meet at lunch, you’ll always have someone available to answer questions and help you navigate your career.You’ll have balance. Meaningful work is only one part of a meaningful life. We offer flexibility and benefits designed to support your well-being — inside and outside of work.You’ll have fun. Yes, we’re accountants and business advisors — but we also like to celebrate, connect, and have a good time. Office events, volunteer opportunities, and casual team activities are all part of the experience. Typical Day in the Life A typical day as a CRM Consulting Intern may include the following: Assist with Salesforce, Microsoft, or integration implementation engagements. Some projects may include writing code/development. Participate in outlining implementation objectives, issues, findings and recommendations in a variety of client situations. Documenting technical solutions. Working with other members of your team to find answers to complex problems. Communicating internally and externally to ensure all parties are operating in unison. Leveraging user stories to test custom built functionality. Who You Are We are seeking a highly-motivated intern to work on our CRM consulting team. Consulting Aptitude Ownership – Able to work independently and proactively, identifying issues and raise them to management, as well as offering potential solutions Communication – Ability to communicate timely and effectively with clients, project managers, team leads, and co-workers Collaboration – Able to work with different departments and teams to maintain productivity and add value Ambition – Initiative to dig into the "why" of various results and a desire to grow responsibility to become a domain expert Problem Solver – Flexibility to handle rapidly changing project priorities and timelines Technical Aptitude You have the desire to learn from consultants how to assess client implementations needs, craft innovative solutions that span different subject matter domains and implement these plans to exceed the client expectations. You work well with technical developers on potential customizations to the project. You have a strong understanding of business acumen. You are working toward a Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Business, Accounting, or other related field. You have a genuine interest in working with CRM applications and cloud-based software implementations, business process consulting, or general systems integration work. You have the ability to effectively maintain and build working relationships with coworkers and clients. You have the ability to work on multiple projects and meet deadlines by setting priorities with projects. Must be authorized to work in the United States now or in the future without visa sponsorship. Other Benefits to working at Eide Bailly Work on real client projects with the guidance of experienced data integration specialists Exposure to a wide breadth of challenges & solutions in multiple industries Exposure to data integrations tools and technologies Eligible for health insurance Potential certification reimbursement What to Expect Next We'll be in touch! If you look like the right fit for our position, one of our recruiters will be reaching out to schedule a phone interview with you to learn more about your career interests and goals. Interns:We are excited to share that intern positions in technology consulting are paid $25.00/hour and are eligible for overtime. Interns are eligible for health insurance and 401(k) Profit Sharing. Eide Bailly LLP is proud to be an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected under local, state or federal laws.

jobs.description: Employer: The Toro Company Expires: 11/07/2026 The 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Candidates must be available to start on May 17 and participate through the duration of the program.Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future. Who Are We? The Toro Company (TTC) has delivered market-leading, innovative products and outstanding customer care for more than 100 years. With over 11,000 employees worldwide, TTC is headquartered in Bloomington, Minnesota, USA.Our company designs and manufactures turf maintenance equipment; turf irrigation systems; landscape and lighting products; snow and ice management solutions; agricultural irrigation systems; rental, specialty and underground construction equipment; and residential turf and snow equipment. jobs.title: Research Intern at Largo US, Inc
jobs.description: Employer: Largo US, Inc Expires: 11/07/2026 Research Intern (Largo US) Largo US is the American arm of Largo, a Swiss-based research and tech company. Who to cast. Who to sign. Who to partner with. What to greenlight. Studios, networks, brands, and agencies make those calls using our E-Score data, which measures how people really feel about the talent, brands, shows, and characters they're betting on. What you'd actually be doing Research lives or dies on the details. This is where you find out how much. Tracking down and formatting assets: images, bios, show infoKeeping our databases current and accurateRunning QC on survey data, trend reports, and open-ended responses (people write wild things in surveys; you'll see)Testing surveys before launch and catching what's brokenKeeping up with pop culture: new shows, rising talent, brand moves You might be a fit if… You sweat the details. A typo, a categorization error, an unusual shift in data trends is exactly what a client notices. We need you to notice it first.You know Excel. Not "I've opened it before." You're comfortable in big spreadsheets, sorting, filtering, formatting, and using formulas. Word too. PowerPoint's a plus, not a requirement.You can do repetitive work without your attention checking out halfway through.You're curious about research, about entertainment, about how these decisions get made behind the scenes.You speak up. If something looks off, you flag it instead of quietly working around it. What you’ll gain: You’ll get hands-on experience with entertainment and brand research, learn how surveys are tested and data is checked, and see how E-Score supports decisions across the industry. You’ll work with an experienced research team and build skills in data quality, survey operations, and research tools.

jobs.description: Employer: RoseMcKenna, PLLC Expires: 11/08/2026 Are you a college student looking to spend your Summer in a meaningful way? We will reach out to those that best meet the qualifications.Please note that interviews are scheduled to begin in early November 2026.Transportation: Convenient to Farragut North and Farragut West Metros (Red, Blue, Orange, and Silver lines). jobs.description: Employer: WSFS Bank Expires: 11/08/2026 Bryn Mawr Trust, a WSFS Company, provides locally managed and collaborative wealth management solutions, including a broad array of planning and advisory services, investment management, trust and estate planning, brokerage and investment services to individual, corporate, and institutional clients through multiple integrated businesses. We are seeking driven and high-performing college students with an interest in financial services to join the WSFS Bank 2027 Wealth Management Summer Internship Program. This paid internship offers meaningful, hands-on experience, professional mentorship, exposure to senior leadership, collaborative project work, volunteer opportunities, and valuable networking experiences. Internship opportunities are available across a variety of Wealth Management departments, including: Endowments and Foundations - This internship provides exposure to Endowment & Foundation services while supporting client meetings, RFP submissions, and other wealth management initiatives. The intern will work closely with advisors and team members, manage multiple priorities, and gain insight into client needs and industry processes. Additional opportunities include participating in committee activities, meeting regularly with mentors, and collaborating on various projects.What Our Internships Offer:Work alongside professionals across multiple business lines and gain exposure to real-world projects, operations, and strategic decision-making.Follow a comprehensive learning program that includes personal and professional development activities and resources.Opportunity to support and present on projects, research, or operational activities within an assigned business area to Senior Leaders.Build meaningful connections through dedicated mentorship and collaboration with peers and experienced professionals.Engage with leaders across the organization through networking events, panel discussions, and career-focused conversations.Participate in volunteer initiatives, employee resource groups, and social exclusive events designed to foster connection and professional growth.High-performing interns may be considered for continued employment opportunities with Bryn Mawr Trust/WSFS Bank upon successful completion of the program. Minimum Qualifications:Must be at least 18 years of age.Pursuing an undergraduate degree with the intention to return to your studies following the internship experience.Must have completed a minimum of one (1) full year of college by May 2027.A business-related or related college major is preferred.Must be able to participate in this full-time position (40 hours per week) within a continuous program, starting first week of June and ending early to mid-August.Must be available for in-person and virtual interviews.Must be available for in person orientation with Human Resources.Ability to work up to 5 days on-site at a physical office location within the WSFS Bank footprint.Must have reliable transportation.Fundamental computer proficiency, including Microsoft Office, is required.Excellent oral and written communication is required.Must have critical thinking and analytical skills.Must have organizational skills and proven ability to work independently and collaboratively. WSFS Bank will only consider candidates who are presently authorized to work for any employer in the United States and who will not require work visa sponsorship from WSFS Bank now or in the future in order to retain their authorization to work in the United States.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Product Manager [Summer 2027 Intern] at Saja
jobs.description: Employer: Saja Expires: 11/08/2026 About SAJASAJA is building a new way to collect, trade, and engage with physical collectibles through a digital-first experience. We're looking for a Product Management Intern for Summer 2027 to own a piece of the product and see it through.What you'll doOwn a project for the summer that ships and matters to the product.Figure out what problem you're solving before deciding what to build.Write things down clearly enough that engineers and designers aren't guessing.Look at how people actually use the product, where they get stuck, and where they leave.Define what success looks like before your project ships, then be honest about the numbers afterward.Talk to users, read support tickets, and spend real time in the product yourself.What we're looking forClear thinking and clear writing. Most of this job is making a fuzzy problem legible to other people.Comfort with data. You don't need to write SQL, but you should be able to look at numbers and work out what they do and don't tell you.Something you've organized, built, or run where you had to make decisions and live with them. A club, a project, an event, a side product.Curiosity about why people behave the way they do, and the instinct to check your assumptions rather than trust them.Willingness to do the unglamorous parts, including support, QA, and writing copy.Interest in consumer products, marketplaces, gaming, collectibles, fintech, or e-commerce.Currently enrolled in a degree program and returning to school after the internship.What this internship is actually likeAt our size, product work is less about process and more about owning a problem until it's solved. You'll write specs, but you'll also chase bugs, answer users, and pull numbers yourself. You'll have someone senior to work through decisions with, and you'll see the effect of what you build quickly, including when it doesn't work.You do not need prior PM experience or a background in collectibles. We care much more about how you think, how clearly you communicate, and whether you finish what you start.For our interview process: Must have a US-based App Store account.Please do not apply to multiple roles within Saja. We will automatically consider you for other roles, but please only apply to one role.

jobs.title: Spring 2027 Communications, Brennan en Español Undergraduate Internship at The Brennan Center for Justice at NYU Law School
jobs.description: Employer: The Brennan Center for Justice at NYU Law School Expires: 11/08/2026 The Brennan Center for Justice at NYU School of Law is a nonpartisan law and policy institute that seeks to improve the systems of democracy and justice in the United States. We work to hold our political institutions and laws accountable to the twin American ideals of democracy and equal justice for all. The Brennan Center’s work ranges from voting rights to campaign finance reform, from ending mass incarceration to preserving constitutional protections in national security policies. Part think tank, part advocacy group, part cutting-edge communications hub, we start with rigorous research. We craft innovative policies. And we fight for them — in Congress and the states, in the courts, and in the court of public opinion. We are seeking interns to join our Communications department on the Brennan en Español team to provide research / writing, and administrative support to staff. Note: This internship is in-person at our New York City office. Responsibilities: All interns will assist with general research and administrative work for the Brennan Center, including coordinating meetings, and drafting routine correspondence. Additionally, there will be opportunities to attend and observe substantive meetings, events, and conversations on program work. In addition to administrative duties, specific responsibilities for the BEE department include: Helping the BEE team with research for different projects, including our newsletter. Writing social media messaging and assisting with social media posting. Contributing to videos for our social media platforms, including helping with writing scripts, and editing and recording of videos. (Experience on-camera is a plus but not required.) Monitoring both coverage in the Spanish-language and Latino press, and announcements and events by Latino organizations. Fluency in both English and Spanish is required. A video assessment will be requested for candidates selected to move forward in the hiring process. Qualifications: The ideal candidates are independent self-starters; detail-oriented; energetic; punctual; and highly organized. Interns must also have excellent research, writing, and analytical skills, as well as a passion for our issues. Experience with Windows, Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Word is a must. Database experience is very helpful. Applicant must be open to evolving responsibilities. We are committed to considering a wide range of candidates, including those with diverse experiences and backgrounds. If you're uncertain about meeting 100% of our qualifications, we encourage you to apply anyway.In your cover letter, please share your interest in the position and what you hope to contribute to the role. This internship is only open to undergraduate students in Spring 2027. Hours: Approximately 10-20 hours per week Pay: $18.40 per hour Duration: Spring Semester 2027 Application Deadline: November 23, 2026 Note: The Brennan Center will follow the rules of your school regarding internships. Therefore, if a school doesn’t allow you to do a paid internship for some reason (i.e., receiving credit, etc.), then your internship will not be paid. In addition, if you are participating in a formal school internship program that allows you to work more than our stated hours, we will make a determination based on our needs and further assessment of your school’s program. To Apply:Please >>LINK HERE<< and upload (preferably in pdf) your (1) resume, (2) cover letter, (3) and a list of contact details for supervisor references. In your cover letter, please specify what interests you about the Brennan en Español team and the Brennan Center for Justice Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage interested students to apply early, as the position will be filled once qualified candidates are found. No phone calls, please. If you have difficulty with the online system, you may send your application by e-mail to brennancenterjobs@nyu.edu with “Spring Brennan en Español Internship” in the subject line, after registering in the online system. Applying through our website is strongly preferred.

jobs.title: Undergraduate Summer Sales Intern at Church & Dwight Co., Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Church & Dwight Co., Inc. Expires: 11/08/2026 Church & Dwight Co., Inc. is offering summer 2027 internship opportunities in our Sales department. This 10-week internship program starts at the end of May and runs through the beginning of August. It includes exposure to leadership, professional development, networking events, and the chance to connect with students throughout various functions. What’s In It for You: Hybrid work schedule (Tues/Wed/Thurs in the office Ewing, NJ) Learning & Development opportunities Summer Speaker Series featuring executive leadership Networking opportunities with early career cohort Access to company store Final Capstone Presentation with leadership Housing Stipend - for students whose residential address is greater than 30 miles from the work site For rising Juniors, this is a multi-year rotational internship planned for Summer 2027 and based on performance a return offer for summer 2028 is considered. For rising Seniors, this is a single-year internship planned for Summer 2028 in available opportunities including Account Management, Sales Strategy, and Revenue Growth Management (RGM). Students must be open to an assignment in any of these areas: Account Management You will work alongside a team of full-time sales associates, who manage a group of named accounts, retain and grow existing client relationships, and forge relationships with prospective clients. In this internship you will: Gain understanding of C&D products, processes and systems Gain understanding of department functions and their responsibilities Assist in attaining annual sales, trade-spending, monthly/quarterly forecast and profit goals Assist in analyzing Syndicated and consumption data to help deliver overall goals Gain insight into overall financial management (Siebel, Trade Spend, Deductions, Slotting, SG&A) Jointly build relationships with external and internal partners to help amplify the voice of the customer Collaborate with various sales departments & cross functional teams to maximize CHD results Gain the ability to influence & impact positive change Sales Strategy You will support the Strategic Business Unit (SBU) team in linking the Brand strategies and plans to the Church and Dwight Field Sales employees. You will support the Sales Strategy Managers within the SBU as they work directly with field sales for an end-to-end plan to manage net sales, trade spending and profitability across all classes of trade within the assigned strategic business unit portfolio of products. The opportunity exists for the intern to directly own aspects of this link with field sales if strong performance is exhibited. In this role you will: Execute strategic trade and brand marketing initiatives across the Category Support the annual Customer / Category Planning process, ensuring that all organizational requirements are met from a timing and data integrity standpoint Manage workflow and information between Category and Field Sales Coordinate the new product development process Collaborate with Sales to develop profitable Trade Spending plans Ensuring Distribution, Shelving, Merchandising and Pricing (DSMP) strategies are accurate and deployed Develop deployment materials for the Sales Playbook Revenue Growth Management (RGM) You will leverage a variety of analytical tools & systems to provide insights and recommendations to improve Customer Promotions and Profitability. The Intern will be responsible for aiding in deep dive analysis into specific categories, brands, channels, and customers to identify key trends as well as competitive insights with the goal of uncovering opportunities to help C&D win in the marketplace. In this role you will: Utilize Trade Promotion Tools to analyze and capture insights from our promotional events to formulate recommendations for our cross functional teams Work across other key Sales Functions including Field Sales and Sales Strategy to collaborate and align on insights to execution across the Revenue Growth Management discipline. Leverage predicative analytic tools to optimize business results for our customer teams Develop exception-based reporting/visualizations to highlight risks and opportunities related to our business and impacts of competition Develop training materials and processes for newly deployed reporting
